scenario: 面试官问：既然有标准 A/B 测试，为什么还要 interleaving、bandit、switchback、准实验这些方法？
scenario_en: Interviewer: if we have standard A/B testing, why do we still need interleaving, bandits, switchback, and quasi-experiments?
q: 为什么需要「超越标准 A/B」的实验方法？
q_en: Why do we need experimentation methods beyond standard A/B?
why: 标准 A/B 在四类生产场景会失效：微小排序差异要几百万用户、动态优化时 50/50 会白烧钱、双边市场共享司机导致干扰、平台级发布无法按用户随机。每一类都有专门方法接手，答对方法体现你懂完整部署生命周期。
why_en: Standard A/B breaks in four production settings — tiny ranking effects, dynamic optimization, marketplace interference, and platform-wide launches — and each has a specialized method.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  F1["微小排序差异"] --> M1["Interleaving"]
  F2["动态优化/短命内容"] --> M2["Multi-armed bandit"]
  F3["双边市场干扰"] --> M3["Switchback"]
  F4["平台级/国家级发布"] --> M4["准实验 DiD/合成控制"]
options: 标准 A/B 只是慢又贵，这些新方法说到底只是换皮的更快版本 A/B，底层机制完全相同、没有本质区别
标准 A/B 在四类场景失效（微小排序差、动态优化、市场干扰、平台级发布），每类有专门方法接手
这些方法已经完全取代了 A/B，以后任何实验都该弃用 A/B、全改用它们，A/B 已彻底过时不再需要
它们只是显著性检验的不同叫法，换个名字，实验设计上并无区别
options_en: Standard A/B is only slow and costly, and these new methods are essentially just repackaged, faster versions of A/B with identical underlying mechanics.
Standard A/B fails in four settings (tiny ranking gaps, dynamic optimization, market interference, platform-wide launches), each with a specialized method.
These methods have fully replaced A/B; every future experiment should abandon A/B entirely and switch to them, since A/B is now completely obsolete.
They are just different names for significance testing, differing only in label, not in experimental design.
optionExplanations: 不是更快的 A/B：interleaving 是被试内设计、bandit 是自适应分配、switchback 是按时间聚类随机，机制根本不同。
对；四种失效场景对应四种方法，选对方法正是「按约束选实验设计」的体现，不是一招通吃。
A/B 仍是测绝对业务指标、做干净因果推断的金标准，新方法各有硬约束，不能全盘取代它。
它们改变的是随机化单元和分配策略（用户 vs 时间窗 vs 自适应），不只是检验名称。
optionExplanations_en: Not faster A/B: interleaving is within-subject, bandits are adaptive allocation, switchback is time-clustered randomization — fundamentally different mechanics.
Correct — four failure settings map to four methods; picking the right one is constraint-driven design, not one-size-fits-all.
A/B is still the gold standard for absolute business metrics and clean causal inference; each new method has hard constraints and can't replace it wholesale.
They change the randomization unit and allocation strategy (user vs time window vs adaptive), not just the test's name.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把用户随机分成两组、各看一个版本，比较绝对指标差异的被试间实验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A/B testing randomly splits users into two arms, each seeing one version, and compares absolute metric differences (a between-subject experiment).

scenario: 你要比较两个排序模型谁更好，但两者质量差异极小，标准 A/B 得几百万用户跑数周才可能测出显著差异。
scenario_en: You must compare two rankers whose quality gap is tiny; standard A/B would need millions of users over weeks to reach significance.
q: 该用标准 A/B 还是 interleaving 来筛这两个排序器？
q_en: Standard A/B or interleaving to screen these two rankers?
why: 微小排序差异用 interleaving：它把两个排序器的结果合并成一个列表给同一个用户，每个用户当自己的对照，消掉巨大的用户间方差，样本效率约 100 倍。标准 A/B 是被试间设计，靠海量样本压方差，太慢太贵。
why_en: Use interleaving for tiny ranking gaps because each user is their own control, killing between-user variance and needing far fewer samples than between-subject A/B.
tradeoff: Interleaving（样本效率高，但只测相对偏好）vs 标准 A/B（可测绝对业务指标，但要海量样本）
whenOtherWins: 当你要的是绝对业务影响（营收、会话时长）而不只是「谁的排序更受欢迎」时，interleaving 测不出，必须回到完整 A/B。
options: 标准 A/B：只有它才能对排序质量给出真正可信的结论，哪怕要几百万用户、连跑上数周也得咬牙跑完，忍一忍就好
都不用，直接看离线 NDCG 谁的分数更高就上线，线上实验的成本和排队时间完全可以省掉
Interleaving：合并两个排序器结果、每用户自己当对照，消掉用户间方差，样本效率约 100 倍
各投一半流量分别做两个独立 A/B，实验结束后再横向比较两个实验各自算出的绝对指标数值
options_en: Standard A/B: only it gives a trustworthy verdict on ranking quality, so even if it takes millions of users over several weeks, just grit your teeth and run it to the end.
Neither — just launch whichever scores higher on offline NDCG and skip online experiments entirely, saving all the cost and queue time.
Interleaving: merge both rankers' results, each user is their own control, killing between-user variance for ~100x sample efficiency.
Run two fully separate A/B tests at half traffic each, then after both finish compare their absolute metric numbers side by side.
optionExplanations: 标准 A/B 能测但极慢：微小差异被巨大用户间方差淹没，得几百万用户数周，成本不划算。
离线 NDCG 与线上真实点击常不一致，跳过线上实验会把「离线好看、线上翻车」的模型放出去。
对；被试内设计让同一用户同时体验两个排序器，方差骤降，是快速初筛排序器的首选。
两个独立 A/B 仍是被试间、仍要海量样本，还多引入实验间不可比问题，没解决方差难题。
optionExplanations_en: A/B can measure it but very slowly: a tiny gap drowns in huge between-user variance, needing millions of users over weeks.
Offline NDCG and real online clicks often diverge; skipping online tests ships models that look good offline but fail live.
Correct — within-subject design lets one user experience both rankers at once, slashing variance, the go-to fast screen for rankers.
Two separate A/B tests are still between-subject and still need huge samples, plus cross-experiment incomparability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把两个排序器的结果混编进同一个列表给同一用户，按点击归因判哪个排序器更受偏好的被试内实验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Interleaving merges two rankers' results into one list for the same user and attributes clicks to decide which ranker is preferred — a within-subject experiment.

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量排序质量的离线指标，越靠前的相关结果得分越高。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG (Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain) is an offline ranking-quality metric that rewards relevant results placed higher.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被试间：不同用户分到不同版本；被试内：同一用户同时体验多个版本、自己当对照。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Between-subject assigns different users to different versions; within-subject exposes the same user to multiple versions as their own control.

scenario: 面试官让你讲清 interleaving 到底怎么运作、为什么样本效率高。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks you to explain exactly how interleaving works and why it is so sample-efficient.
q: Interleaving 的核心机制是什么？
q_en: What is interleaving's core mechanism?
why: 把排序器 A、B 的结果交错合并成一个列表展示给同一用户，用户点了哪个结果就把功劳记给贡献它的排序器；因为同一用户同时看到两者、当自己的对照，用户间的口味差异被抵消，方差骤降。
why_en: Interleave A's and B's results into one list for the same user and credit each click to its source ranker, so each user is their own control and between-user taste variance cancels out.
diagram:
flowchart TB A["排序器 A 结果"] --> M["交错合并成一个列表"] B["排序器 B 结果"] --> M M --> U["同一用户浏览+点击"] U --> C["点击归因给贡献的排序器
点击多者胜"]
options: 把 A、B 结果交错合并成一个列表给同一用户，点击归因给贡献的排序器，每用户自己当对照
把用户随机分成 A 组和 B 组各看一个排序器，跑满整个实验周期后再比两组的平均点击率
先用 A 服务一周、再用 B 服务下一周，事后前后对比这两周各自的点击率高低
让人工标注员离线给两个排序结果打分，取平均分高的排序器
options_en: Interleave A's and B's results into one list for the same user, attribute clicks to the source ranker, each user their own control.
Randomly split users into group A and group B, each sees one ranker, run the full experiment period, then compare the two groups' average click rate.
Serve A for one week, then B for the following week, and afterward compare the two weeks' click rates against each other.
Have human annotators score both ranked lists offline and pick the ranker with the higher average.
optionExplanations: 对；合并成一个列表 + 同一用户当对照，正是消掉用户间方差、拿到 ~100 倍样本效率的关键。
这是标准 A/B（被试间），不同用户看不同版本，方差高，恰恰是 interleaving 要改进的对象。
前后分时段对比会被时间趋势污染（周中 vs 周末），不是 interleaving，也不控制混淆。
离线人工打分不是 interleaving，也测不到真实用户在线点击行为。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — one merged list plus same-user control is exactly what cancels between-user variance for ~100x efficiency.
That's standard A/B (between-subject); different users see different versions, high variance — what interleaving improves on.
Before/after time comparison is polluted by temporal trends (midweek vs weekend), not interleaving and uncontrolled for confounders.
Offline human scoring isn't interleaving and can't capture real online click behavior.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在合并列表里，用户点击某结果时把功劳记给最初产出该结果的排序器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Click attribution credits a click on a result in the merged list to whichever ranker originally produced that result.

scenario: 有人引用「interleaving 比 A/B 少用约 100 倍样本」这个数，问你能不能当成通用常数直接照搬。
scenario_en: Someone cites 'interleaving needs ~100x fewer samples than A/B' and asks whether you can treat it as a universal constant.
q: 「约 100 倍样本效率」这个数该怎么理解？
q_en: How should you read the '~100x sample efficiency' number?
why: ~100× 是 Netflix、微软等报告的经验观察值、不是公式推导，来源是「被试内消掉用户间方差」这一机制，具体倍数取决于方差结构，会随任务变化。所以它是量级直觉（省一两个数量级），不能当固定常数照抄进容量估算。
why_en: The ~100x is an empirical Netflix/Microsoft observation, not a formula — it comes from within-subject variance cancellation and varies with the variance structure, so treat it as an order-of-magnitude intuition, not a constant.
options: 它是精确常数，任何 interleaving 实验都恰好省 100 倍样本，可直接写进样本量公式
它是理论上限，实际永远达不到，最多省 2-3 倍
它是经验观察值（来自 Netflix/微软），源于消掉用户间方差，倍数随方差结构变化，只是量级直觉
它指 interleaving 慢 100 倍，是它相对 A/B 的最大缺点
options_en: It's an exact constant; every interleaving experiment saves exactly 100x samples, safe to plug into a sample-size formula.
It's a theoretical ceiling never reached in practice; you get at most 2-3x in reality.
It's an empirical Netflix/Microsoft observation from variance cancellation; the factor varies with variance structure — an order-of-magnitude intuition.
It means interleaving is 100x slower, its biggest drawback versus A/B.

termDefinitions.meaning: 指标里由用户间差异 vs 版本差异各占多少方差；interleaving 越能消掉的用户间方差占比越大，省样本越多。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Variance structure is how much of a metric's variance comes from between-user vs between-version differences; the more between-user variance interleaving cancels, the more samples it saves.

optionExplanations: 当成精确公式就错了：真实省几倍会随任务波动，没人能保证每次都刚好 100 倍。
把它当成够不到的理论上限也不对，因为 100 倍本身就是从真实产品里量出来的效应，不是空想的上限。
对，它就是一线大厂测出来的经验数字，只当经验参考、别当成放之四海皆准的常数。
跟变慢没关系——这个数说的是能少用多少样本，不是运行时间变长。
optionExplanations_en: Treating it as an exact formula is wrong — real savings swing by task, so no one can guarantee precisely 100x every time.
Calling it an unreachable ceiling misses the point too, since that 100x is itself a number measured from real products, not a fantasy limit.
Correct — it's a number teams like Netflix and Microsoft actually measured, useful as a rough guide but never a plug-in number.
Has nothing to do with slowness — this number is about how few samples you need, not how long anything runs.

scenario: 要实现 interleaving，需要一个公平地把两个排序器的结果交错、并判定胜者的算法。
scenario_en: To implement interleaving you need an algorithm that fairly interleaves two rankers' results and decides a winner.
q: Interleaving 里最常用的 Team Draft 算法怎么判胜负？
q_en: How does the common Team Draft interleaving algorithm decide a winner?
why: Team Draft 像选球队：两个排序器轮流从各自列表里「挑人」放进合并列表，记住每个位置来自谁；用户点击后，跨众多用户统计哪个排序器被归因的点击更多，谁多谁胜。它是最常用的交错方式，保证位置分配大体公平。
why_en: Team Draft alternately 'drafts' picks from each ranker into one list, tracks each slot's source, and the ranker credited with more clicks across users wins.
options: 只看合并列表里谁的第一条结果被点击，就直接判那个排序器赢，把其余所有位置上的点击信号全部忽略掉
两排序器轮流从各自列表挑结果进合并列表并记录来源，跨用户统计被归因点击多者胜
把两个列表拼接后整体随机打乱，看用户点在拼接后的前半段还是后半段
按两个排序器的离线 NDCG 谁高判谁赢，点击只作参考
options_en: Whoever's first result in the merged list gets clicked wins outright, throwing away the click signals from every other position entirely.
The two rankers alternately draft results into the merged list, recording each source; the ranker with more attributed clicks across users wins.
Concatenate both lists, shuffle the whole thing randomly, and see whether users click into the first half or the second half.
Decide by whichever ranker has higher offline NDCG; clicks are only a tiebreaker.
optionExplanations: 只看第一条丢掉了绝大多数信号，位置偏置也会主导结果，不是 Team Draft 的做法。
对；轮流挑选保证位置公平、来源可追溯，再靠跨用户的点击归因累计判胜，是最常用的 interleaving 算法。
随机打乱破坏了公平的位置分配，也无法把点击干净归因到某个排序器。
离线 NDCG 是离线指标；interleaving 的整个意义就是用真实在线点击来判，不靠离线分。
optionExplanations_en: Looking only at the first result throws away most signal and lets position bias dominate — not Team Draft.
Correct — alternating drafts keep positions fair and sources traceable, then attributed clicks accumulated across users decide — the most common interleaving algorithm.
Random shuffling breaks fair position assignment and prevents clean per-ranker attribution.
Offline NDCG is offline; interleaving's whole point is judging by real online clicks, not offline scores.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最常用的 interleaving 交错算法：两个排序器轮流从各自结果里挑一条放入合并列表，点击归因后点击多者胜。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Team Draft is the most common interleaving algorithm: two rankers alternately draft one result each into the merged list, and the one credited with more clicks wins.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户更倾向点靠前的结果，与内容相关性无关；公平的交错设计要抵消它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Position bias is users' tendency to click higher-ranked results regardless of relevance; fair interleaving must offset it.

scenario: 有人想把 interleaving 当唯一的上线判据，你要说清它的适用边界。
scenario_en: Someone wants interleaving as the sole launch criterion; you must lay out where it stops applying.
q: Interleaving 有哪些固有局限？(多选)
q_en: What are interleaving's inherent limitations? (multiple)
why: 三条局限：只测「相对偏好」给不出营收/会话时长等绝对业务指标；只适用排序/推荐这类可交错的界面；单会话设计抓不到长期行为变化（如新奇效应消退）。因此它是初筛器，最终仍要 A/B 收口。GPU 成本与它无关。
why_en: Interleaving only measures relative preference, only fits rankable surfaces, and single-session design misses long-term shifts, so it screens candidates but A/B still closes the decision.
options: 只能测相对偏好，给不出营收、会话时长等绝对业务指标
只适用排序/推荐这类结果可交错的界面
单会话设计，抓不到长期行为变化（如新奇效应消退、留存）
需要更多 GPU 才能运行，是它比 A/B 更贵的主要原因
options_en: Measures only relative preference, giving no absolute business metrics like revenue or session length.
Only fits rankable surfaces like ranking/recommendation where results can be interleaved.
Single-session design misses long-term behavioral shifts (novelty fading, retention).
It needs more GPUs to run, the main reason it costs more than A/B.
optionExplanations: 对；它只告诉你「哪个排序更受偏好」，测不出这偏好是否转化为营收或时长，绝对指标得靠 A/B。
对；交错要求两套结果能合并成一个列表，购物车、结账等非排序界面无法这样交错。
对；一次会话内的偏好抓不到几周后的行为变化，长期效应仍需 A/B 观察窗。
错；interleaving 反而更省样本、更便宜，GPU 成本不是它的局限。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — it tells you which ranking is preferred but not whether that converts to revenue or time; absolute metrics need A/B.
Correct — interleaving requires two result sets mergeable into one list; non-ranking surfaces like carts or checkout can't interleave.
Correct — one session's preference can't capture behavioral change weeks later, so long-term effects still need an A/B window.
Wrong — interleaving is cheaper and more sample-efficient; GPU cost is not its limitation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户对新功能一开始的短暂追捧，随时间消退；单会话实验容易被它误导。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The novelty effect is users' brief initial enthusiasm for a new feature that fades over time, which single-session experiments can mistake for real gains.

scenario: 你有 10 个候选排序器，想又快又稳地选出最终上线的那个。面试里怎么组合 interleaving 和 A/B？
scenario_en: You have 10 candidate rankers and want to pick the launch one quickly yet reliably; how do you combine interleaving and A/B?
q: 把「interleaving 初筛 → A/B 收口」的两阶段流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the two-stage 'interleaving screen then A/B confirm' funnel:
steps: 用 interleaving 快速初筛，凭相对偏好淘汰明显更差的排序器
把候选缩到 1-2 个 finalist
对 finalist 跑完整 A/B，测营收/留存等绝对业务影响
按绝对指标做最终上线决策
why: 先用便宜的 interleaving 从一堆候选里快速砍到 1-2 个，再对少数 finalist 花贵的完整 A/B 测绝对影响、做上线决策。这样既拿到 interleaving 的速度，又保住 A/B 的绝对可信度，是漏斗式取信号。
why_en: Use cheap interleaving to narrow many candidates to 1-2 finalists, then spend a full A/B on those to measure absolute impact and decide — a funnel combining interleaving's speed with A/B's trustworthiness.
diagram:
flowchart LR N["10 候选排序器"] --> I["interleaving 初筛
相对偏好"] I --> F["1-2 个 finalist"] F --> AB["完整 A/B
绝对影响"] AB --> D["上线决策"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 经初筛后进入最终评估的少数候选方案，只对它们花昂贵的完整实验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A finalist is one of the few candidates surviving screening, on which you spend the expensive full experiment.

scenario: 面试官问：多臂老虎机（MAB）跟固定 50/50 的 A/B 到底有什么本质区别？
scenario_en: Interviewer: how is a multi-armed bandit (MAB) fundamentally different from a fixed 50/50 A/B?
q: 多臂老虎机（MAB）相对固定 A/B 的核心差别是什么？
q_en: What is a MAB's core difference from a fixed A/B?
why: MAB 在实验进行中就把流量动态倾斜向表现更好的 arm，而不是全程固定 50/50。这样能边学边少烧钱在差 arm 上，代价是分配随时间变化（非平稳），让固定终点的统计推断变难。
why_en: A MAB shifts traffic toward the better arm mid-experiment instead of a fixed 50/50, spending less on losers but making fixed-horizon inference harder.
options: MAB 也全程固定 50/50，只是最后用不同公式算显著性
MAB 需要更多 arm，至少 8 个才能启动，2 个 arm 用不了
MAB 在实验中动态把流量倾向表现更好的 arm，而非固定 50/50
MAB 只能离线跑，不能在线分配真实流量
options_en: A MAB also stays a fixed 50/50 throughout and just uses a different formula for significance at the end.
A MAB needs more arms, at least 8 to start, and can't run with only 2 arms.
A MAB dynamically shifts traffic toward the better-performing arm mid-experiment rather than a fixed 50/50.
A MAB can only run offline and cannot allocate real online traffic.
optionExplanations: 固定 50/50 正是 A/B 的做法，MAB 的整个卖点就是打破它、自适应分配。
MAB 对 arm 数没有下限，2 个 arm 也能跑；多 arm 只是它相对 A/B 的一个优势场景。
对；动态倾斜流量让它「边服务边学习」、减少累计后悔值，代价是分配非平稳。
MAB 就是在线自适应分配真实流量的框架，不是离线方法。
optionExplanations_en: Fixed 50/50 is exactly what A/B does; a MAB's whole point is to break it with adaptive allocation.
A MAB has no minimum arm count; 2 arms work fine, and many arms is just one of its advantage cases.
Correct — dynamic traffic shifting lets it 'learn while serving' and cut cumulative regret, at the cost of non-stationary allocation.
A MAB is precisely an online framework that adaptively allocates real traffic, not an offline method.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多臂老虎机：在多个候选（arm）间自适应分配流量、边学边把流量导向更优 arm 的实验框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MAB (Multi-Armed Bandit) is an experiment framework that adaptively allocates traffic across arms, learning and shifting traffic toward better arms.

termDefinitions.meaning: 老虎机里的一个候选选项（如一个版本/一条 headline），MAB 要决定给每个 arm 多少流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An arm is one candidate option (a version/headline); the MAB decides how much traffic each arm gets.

scenario: MAB 每一步都要决定：给已知最好的 arm 更多流量，还是给不确定的 arm 一些流量去多了解它？
scenario_en: At each step a MAB must decide: send more traffic to the known-best arm, or give uncertain arms traffic to learn about them?
q: MAB 里的 exploration vs exploitation 张力是什么，累计后悔值指什么？
q_en: What is the exploration-vs-exploitation tension in a MAB, and what is cumulative regret?
why: Exploitation 把流量给当前最好的 arm 拿即时收益，exploration 分流量给不确定 arm 以免错过最优；累计后悔值是没选到最优 arm 而损失的总奖励，MAB 要把它压到最小。
why_en: Exploitation sends traffic to the currently best arm for immediate reward, exploration samples uncertain arms to avoid missing the true best, and cumulative regret is the total reward lost by not always picking the optimal arm.
tradeoff: Exploitation（拿即时收益，但可能错过更好的 arm）vs exploration（多了解 arm，但短期烧掉一些奖励）
options: Exploitation 给当前最好 arm 拿即时收益，exploration 分流量给不确定 arm；后悔值=没选到最优 arm 损失的总奖励
Exploration 指往候选列表里不断多加新的 arm，exploitation 指把表现差的 arm 逐个删掉，后悔值就是整个实验里被删掉的 arm 的总数量
两者是同义词，都指把流量全给最好的 arm，后悔值指实验总时长
Exploitation 是随机分配，exploration 是固定 50/50，后悔值是 p 值大小
options_en: Exploitation sends traffic to the current best arm for immediate reward, exploration samples uncertain arms; regret = total reward lost by not picking the optimal arm.
Exploration means continually adding new arms to the candidate list, exploitation means deleting the weak arms one by one, and regret is the total count of arms deleted over the whole experiment.
They are synonyms, both meaning give all traffic to the best arm, and regret is the total experiment duration.
Exploitation is random allocation, exploration is a fixed 50/50, and regret is the size of the p-value.
optionExplanations: 对；这正是 MAB 的核心张力，最小化累计后悔值就是在「即时收益」和「信息获取」之间动态平衡。
exploration/exploitation 说的是流量分配策略，不是增删 arm；后悔值是损失的奖励不是 arm 数。
两者是对立而非同义：全给最好 arm 是纯 exploitation，会因估计错误吃亏。
把定义完全对调了，且后悔值与 p 值是两个不同概念。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — this is the MAB's core tension; minimizing cumulative regret balances immediate reward against information gain.
Exploration/exploitation are traffic-allocation strategies, not adding/removing arms; regret is lost reward, not arm count.
They are opposites, not synonyms: giving all traffic to the best arm is pure exploitation and suffers from estimation error.
It swaps the definitions and confuses regret with the p-value.

termDefinitions.meaning: 整个实验里因为没有始终选中真正最优 arm 而少拿到的奖励总和；MAB 的优化目标是最小化它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cumulative regret is the total reward lost over the experiment by not always choosing the truly optimal arm; the MAB minimizes it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 探索：分流量给不确定 arm 以获取信息；利用：把流量给当前估计最好的 arm 拿即时收益。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Exploration sends traffic to uncertain arms for information; exploitation sends it to the current best arm for immediate reward.

scenario: 选一个 bandit 分配策略，你在 epsilon-greedy、UCB、Thompson Sampling 之间权衡探索方式。
scenario_en: Choosing a bandit allocation strategy, you weigh how epsilon-greedy, UCB, and Thompson Sampling explore.
q: epsilon-greedy、UCB、Thompson Sampling 的探索机制分别是什么？
q_en: How do epsilon-greedy, UCB, and Thompson Sampling each explore?
why: epsilon-greedy 以 ε 概率随机探索；UCB 给估计奖励加随样本缩小的置信奖励、定向探不确定 arm；Thompson 按奖励后验分布采样选 arm，工业最常用。
why_en: Epsilon-greedy explores randomly with probability epsilon, UCB adds a shrinking confidence bonus to favor uncertain arms, and Thompson Sampling samples from a Bayesian posterior over each arm's reward rate.
tradeoff: epsilon-greedy（简单但盲目探索）vs UCB（定向探不确定 arm）vs Thompson（贝叶斯采样，探索自然衰减）

rows: 以 ε 概率随机探
加置信奖励，随样本缩小

options: 三者其实都是固定 50/50 分配流量到实验结束，只是最后算显著性时公式名字不同
epsilon-greedy 随机探索、UCB 用置信奖励定向探、Thompson 按后验采样选 arm
epsilon-greedy 其实是贝叶斯方法、UCB 完全不做任何探索、Thompson 全靠随机数瞎猜，三者互不相关也没有共同框架
三者都要求先跑完整 A/B 才能启动，属于 A/B 的后处理步骤
options_en: All three actually hold a fixed 50/50 allocation until the experiment ends, differing only in the name of the significance formula at the end.
Epsilon-greedy explores randomly, UCB uses a confidence bonus to target exploration, Thompson samples from the posterior.
Epsilon-greedy is actually the Bayesian method, UCB does no exploration whatsoever, and Thompson relies purely on random guessing — the three are unrelated with no shared framework.
All three require a full A/B to finish first, being post-processing steps of A/B.
optionExplanations: 固定 50/50 是 A/B，不是 bandit；三者的分配都是自适应的。
对；三者探索方式不同——盲目随机、置信上界定向、后验采样，越往后探索越「聪明」，Thompson 工业最常用。
说反了：贝叶斯是 Thompson，UCB 靠置信奖励主动探索，三者都在做探索/利用平衡。
bandit 是独立框架，不是 A/B 的后处理，也不需要先跑完 A/B。
optionExplanations_en: Fixed 50/50 is A/B, not a bandit; all three allocate adaptively.
Correct — the three explore differently: blind random, upper-confidence targeting, posterior sampling, getting smarter in that order, with Thompson most used industrially.
Backwards: Bayesian is Thompson, UCB actively explores via a confidence bonus, and all three balance explore/exploit.
Bandits are a standalone framework, not A/B post-processing, and don't require a finished A/B.

termDefinitions.meaning: 以 1−ε 概率选当前最好 arm、以 ε 概率随机探索其他 arm 的简单 bandit 策略。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Epsilon-greedy picks the current best arm with probability 1 minus epsilon and explores a random arm with probability epsilon.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给每个 arm 的估计奖励加一个随样本增多而缩小的置信奖励，优先探索不确定的 arm。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UCB (Upper Confidence Bound) adds a confidence bonus, shrinking as samples grow, to each arm's estimated reward, favoring uncertain arms.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为每个 arm 的奖励率维护后验分布，每次从后验采样再选采样值最高的 arm 的贝叶斯策略。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Thompson Sampling keeps a posterior over each arm's reward rate and samples from it to choose an arm — a Bayesian strategy.

scenario: 一条突发新闻只在 6 小时内相关，你有 8 个标题变体，目标是最大化这段时间的总点击率（CTR）。
scenario_en: A breaking story is relevant for only 6 hours; you have 8 headline variants and want to maximize total CTR over that window.
q: 这种「短命、多变体、要最大化总收益」的场景该用哪种实验？
q_en: Which experiment fits a short-lived, many-variant, maximize-total-reward scenario?
why: 用带 Thompson Sampling 的多臂老虎机：6 小时窗口太短，A/B 固定 50/50 会把曝光浪费在差标题上，8 个变体等分更吃不饱样本；bandit 边学边导流，直接最大化总 CTR。
why_en: Use a multi-armed bandit with Thompson Sampling because the 6-hour window is too short for a fixed 50/50 A/B, and adaptive allocation shifts traffic to the best of 8 headlines to maximize total CTR.
tradeoff: Bandit（边学边赚、少烧差 arm，但固定终点推断难）vs A/B（干净因果，但短窗+多变体下浪费曝光）
whenOtherWins: 如果目标是拿到一个能长期复用、可做严格因果推断的绝对结论（而非最大化这一次的总收益），标准 A/B 的干净 p 值更合适。
options: 标准 A/B，把 8 个变体各分 1/8 固定流量，等跑满 6 小时收集完全部数据后再统一比较谁的 CTR 最高
带 Thompson Sampling 的多臂老虎机，边学边把流量导向表现好的标题，最大化窗口内总 CTR
Interleaving，把 8 个标题两两交错进同一个列表，靠点击归因比出相对偏好谁更受欢迎
Switchback，按城市或时间段每 30 分钟在 8 个标题间整体切换一次，观察哪个窗口点击率更高
options_en: Standard A/B: give each of the 8 variants a fixed 1/8 of traffic, run the full 6 hours, collect all the data, and only then compare whose CTR is highest.
A multi-armed bandit with Thompson Sampling, learning and shifting traffic to the best headline to maximize total CTR in the window.
Interleaving: merge all 8 headlines pairwise into one shared list and use click attribution to rank relative preference among them.
Switchback: switch the whole city or time segment among the 8 headlines every 30 minutes and see which window gets a higher click rate.
optionExplanations: 8 等分 + 固定分配意味着到实验结束才收敛，6 小时里大半曝光烧在差标题上，总 CTR 被拖低。
对；6 小时窗口配 8 个标题正是 bandit 的主场——流量会自动倾向点击好的那条，总点击不会被差标题拖累。
interleaving 只测「哪个更受偏好」的相对信号，不最大化总收益，也不适合 8 个并列文本变体。
switchback 是给双边市场干扰设计的（按时间/地域切），这里没有司机共享池，用错了工具。
optionExplanations_en: An 8-way even split with fixed allocation only converges at the end, wasting most impressions on weak headlines over 6 hours.
Correct — a 6-hour window with 8 headlines is exactly a bandit's home turf: traffic drifts on its own toward whichever headline clicks best, so nothing gets wasted on the losers.
Interleaving measures relative preference, not total reward, and doesn't fit 8 parallel text variants.
Switchback is for marketplace interference (switching by time/region); with no shared driver pool, it's the wrong tool.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击率：展示中被点击的比例，这里是要在 6 小时内最大化的目标奖励。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CTR (Click-Through Rate) is the fraction of impressions clicked, here the reward to maximize within 6 hours.

scenario: 你用 bandit 跑了一个实验，想在结束时像 A/B 一样报一个 p 值下结论。
scenario_en: You ran a bandit experiment and want to report an end-of-experiment p-value like an A/B.
why: bandit 的自适应分配是非平稳的（各 arm 流量随时间变），违背固定终点检验假设的等概率、独立同分布，直接算末尾 p 值不成立、会给出错误显著性。缓解方向是专门设计，如混合自适应设计（MAD）在自适应分配里保留可做有效推断的部分。
why_en: Bandit allocation is non-stationary, which invalidates fixed-horizon p-values, so use designs like mixture adaptive design (MAD) that preserve valid inference.
q: 为什么 bandit 让「实验结束算 p 值」这件事变得不可靠？怎么补救？
q_en: Why do bandits make end-of-experiment p-values unreliable, and how do you fix it?
options: 非平稳的自适应分配违背固定终点检验假设，末尾 p 值失效；用混合自适应设计（MAD）保留可推断部分
bandit 的 p 值天然更准，因为样本都集中在表现好的 arm 上、噪声更少，末尾直接算就行，无需任何额外补救
问题只是样本不够多，把实验时长翻倍、样本堆够，末尾 p 值就恢复有效
bandit 根本不产生任何指标，无所谓 p 值，直接看总奖励即可，不存在推断问题
options_en: Non-stationary adaptive allocation violates fixed-horizon test assumptions, invalidating end p-values; use mixture adaptive design (MAD) to preserve valid inference.
Bandit p-values are naturally more accurate because samples concentrate on the better-performing arms with less noise, so you can just compute one at the end with no extra fix needed.
It's only a sample-size issue; double the duration and pile on samples and the end p-value becomes valid again.
Bandits produce no metrics at all, so p-values are irrelevant — just read total reward; there is no inference problem.
optionExplanations: 对；非平稳分配破坏了固定终点检验对等概率、独立同分布的假设，MAD 这类设计专门在自适应中留出可做有效推断的结构。
样本集中在好 arm 恰恰让分布非平稳、推断更难，不是更准。
堆样本不解决非平稳这个结构问题；p 值失效是分配随时间变导致的，不是样本量不够。
bandit 当然有指标（奖励、CTR），只是固定终点推断需要特殊处理，不能说没有推断问题。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — non-stationary allocation breaks the equal-probability, i.i.d. assumptions of fixed-horizon tests; MAD preserves a structure for valid inference.
Concentrating samples on good arms is exactly what makes the distribution non-stationary and inference harder, not more accurate.
More samples don't fix the structural non-stationarity; p-values fail because allocation changes over time, not from too few samples.
Bandits do have metrics (reward, CTR); fixed-horizon inference just needs special handling, so the problem is real.

termDefinitions.term: fixed-horizon inference / 固定终点推断
termDefinitions.meaning: 在预先设定的样本量/时间点上做一次显著性检验（如 A/B 的末尾 p 值），要求分配平稳、独立同分布。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fixed-horizon inference runs one significance test at a preset sample size or time (like A/B's end p-value), assuming stationary, i.i.d. allocation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 混合自适应设计：在自适应分配里混入一部分可做有效统计推断的结构，缓解 bandit 破坏 p 值的问题。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MAD (Mixture Adaptive Design) blends a share of statistically valid structure into adaptive allocation to restore inference under bandits.

scenario: 面试里要一句话点出 bandit 和 A/B 各自「为什么而生」。
scenario_en: In an interview, capture in one line what bandits vs A/B each optimize for.
q: 一句话对比：bandit 和 A/B 各自优化的是什么？
q_en: In one line, what do bandits vs A/B each optimize?
why: bandit 优化「边服务边学习」——在实验期就尽量多赚、少烧差 arm；A/B 优化「干净的因果测量」——牺牲实验期收益换一个可信、可推断的绝对结论。选哪个取决于你更在意实验期收益还是结论的因果纯度。
why_en: Bandits optimize learning-while-serving (earn during the experiment), while A/B optimizes clean causal measurement (a trustworthy absolute conclusion).
tradeoff: Bandit（实验期收益最大化，但因果推断难）vs A/B（干净因果结论，但实验期要付浪费成本）
options: 两者都只优化统计功效，唯一区别是 bandit 更快
bandit 优化实验期总收益，A/B 其实也在优化实验期总收益，只是分配比例不同，二者的根本目标完全一致
bandit 优化「边服务边学习」的实验期收益，A/B 优化「干净的因果测量」
A/B 优化实验期收益、bandit 优化因果纯度，正好相反
options_en: Both optimize only statistical power, differing only in that bandits are faster.
Bandits optimize in-experiment total reward, and A/B actually optimizes in-experiment total reward too, just with a different split ratio — their fundamental goal is identical.
Bandits optimize in-experiment reward (learning while serving); A/B optimizes clean causal measurement.
A/B optimizes in-experiment reward and bandits optimize causal purity — exactly reversed.
optionExplanations: 统计功效只是 A/B 关心的一面；bandit 关心的是实验期少烧钱，两者目标根本不同。
A/B 不优化实验期收益——它固定 50/50、甘愿在差 arm 上付浪费成本换干净结论。
对；这就是那句可带走的对比——bandit 边赚边学，A/B 用实验期成本买因果纯度。
方向说反了：bandit 才是优化实验期收益的那个，A/B 才是买因果纯度的那个。
optionExplanations_en: Statistical power is only one A/B concern; a bandit's goal is spending less mid-experiment — different objectives.
A/B doesn't optimize in-experiment reward — it holds 50/50 and pays the waste to buy a clean conclusion.
Correct — that's the takeaway line: bandits earn while learning, A/B pays in-experiment cost for causal purity.
Reversed: bandits optimize in-experiment reward, and A/B buys causal purity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把结果差异干净地归因到「版本」这一处理变量，而非人群或时间的混淆，A/B 的核心价值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Causal measurement cleanly attributes an outcome difference to the treatment (the version) rather than population or time confounders — A/B's core value.

scenario: Uber/DoorDash 想测新定价。骑手和司机共享同一个司机池：给一半骑手涨价会改变另一半（对照组）能叫到的车，两组不再独立。
scenario_en: Uber/DoorDash want to test new pricing. Riders share one driver pool: pricing up for half the riders changes car availability for the other (control) half, so arms aren't independent.
q: 这种共享司机池的双边市场该用哪种实验设计？
q_en: Which design fits a shared-driver-pool marketplace?
why: 用 switchback：按用户随机会因共享司机池干扰、违背 SUTVA，估计有偏；改成按「城市 × 30-60 分钟时间窗」整体切换处理——随机化单位是区域-时间块，不是用户数，块内所有人同处理、消掉干扰。
why_en: Use switchback because user-level randomization causes interference via the shared driver pool, violating SUTVA; instead randomize time windows within a region so everyone in a city-time block gets the same arm.
tradeoff: Switchback（消掉市场干扰，但有跨窗残留效应）vs 用户级 A/B（干净随机，但共享供给下干扰致偏）
whenOtherWins: 如果处理不共享稀缺供给、一个用户的体验不影响另一个用户（如纯前端 UI 改动），普通用户级 A/B 就够，不必上 switchback。
options: 用户级 A/B：把骑手随机分成两组、各自只看一种定价方案，实现起来简单直接、上线也快
Switchback：在地理区域内按时间窗随机，城市每 30-60 分钟整体切换处理，块内所有人同处理
Interleaving：把两种定价方案交错展示给同一个骑手，让他在同一次下单流程里同时看到两种价格再择优
准实验 DiD：直接拿涨价的城市和没涨价的城市的完单率指标做事后对比，不做任何随机化
options_en: User-level A/B: randomly split riders into two groups, each seeing only one pricing scheme — simple, direct, and quick to ship.
Switchback: randomize time windows within a region; a city switches its arm every 30-60 minutes, everyone in a block gets the same arm.
Interleaving: interleave the two pricing schemes for the same rider so they see both prices at once within a single order flow and pick the better one.
Quasi-experiment DiD: just compare completion-rate metrics between a price-raised city and a non-raised city after the fact, no randomization at all.
optionExplanations: 用户级 A/B 正是问题所在：共享司机池让处理组抢走对照组的车，两组不独立，估计有偏。
对；按城市-时间块整体切换消掉块内干扰，是共享供给市场做因果实验的标准招。
定价不能像排序结果那样交错展示给同一人，interleaving 在这里没有意义。
DiD 是没法随机时的准实验兜底；这里能主动做随机（按时间/地域），switchback 比事后观察更可信。
optionExplanations_en: User-level A/B is the very problem: the shared pool lets treatment steal cars from control, so arms aren't independent and estimates are biased.
Correct — switching whole city-time blocks removes within-block interference, the standard causal design for shared-supply markets.
Prices can't be interleaved to one person like ranked results; interleaving is meaningless here.
DiD is the fallback when randomization is impossible; here you can randomize by time/region, so switchback beats after-the-fact observation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在地理区域内按时间窗随机的实验：一个区域每隔一段时间整体在 treatment/控制间切换，用来消掉共享供给下的干扰。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A switchback experiment randomizes time windows within a region, switching the whole region between treatment and control periodically to remove shared-supply interference.

termDefinitions.meaning: 稳定单元处理值假设：一个单元的结果只取决于它自己受的处理，不受别人处理影响；共享司机池会破坏它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SUTVA (Stable Unit Treatment Value Assumption) says a unit's outcome depends only on its own treatment, not others'; a shared driver pool breaks it.

scenario: 在共享司机池的市场里坚持按骑手随机分组，测新定价对完单率的影响。
scenario_en: In a shared-driver-pool market you insist on rider-level randomization to test new pricing's effect on completion rate.
q: 共享供给下按用户随机会出什么问题，后果是什么？
q_en: What goes wrong with user-level randomization under shared supply, and what's the consequence?
why: 违背 SUTVA 的干扰：处理组涨价改变的是共享司机池的可用运力（供给单位，不是骑手账户数），连带影响对照组骑手能叫到的车。后果是处理效应≈定价效应+供给扰动，两者分不开，估计有偏。
why_en: It violates SUTVA — treatment riders alter the shared pool's availability, so control riders' outcomes shift too, contaminating the estimate so you can't separate the pricing effect from disturbed supply.
options: 没问题，只要样本量足够大，干扰造成的这点偏差就会自己相互抵消掉，估计仍然是无偏的
处理组涨价改变共享司机池可用性、连带影响对照组结果，违背 SUTVA，处理效应被污染、估计有偏
问题只是运行得慢，只要多等几天、让数据积累得更多，估计自然就会变准
唯一的后果是对照组骑手的体验意外变好了，于是处理效应会被系统性地低估一些，但正负方向的判断应该仍然是正确的
options_en: No problem — with a large enough sample this bit of interference bias will cancel itself out, and the estimate stays unbiased.
Treatment pricing alters shared-pool availability and spills into control outcomes, violating SUTVA; the treatment effect is contaminated and biased.
It's only slow; wait a few more days for more data to accumulate and the estimate will naturally become accurate.
The only consequence is that control-group riders' experience accidentally improves, so the treatment effect gets systematically underestimated, but the sign of the direction should still be correct.
optionExplanations: 干扰不会随样本变大而抵消——它是系统性偏差，样本再大也偏。
对；处理泄漏到对照组正是 SUTVA 被破坏的表现，指标变化混入了供给扰动，无法干净归因。
这不是速度问题：偏差来自结构性干扰，等再久数据也偏。
干扰方向和大小都不确定，不能假定只是「低估但方向对」，可能整个符号都错。
optionExplanations_en: Interference doesn't cancel with larger samples — it's a systematic bias that persists.
Correct — treatment spilling into control is exactly the SUTVA violation; the metric change mixes in supply disturbance and can't be cleanly attributed.
Not a speed issue: the bias is structural interference, so waiting longer stays biased.
The interference's sign and size are uncertain; you can't assume merely 'underestimated but right direction' — even the sign may flip.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个单元受到的处理影响到另一个单元的结果，常见于共享资源（司机池、库存）的场景，破坏独立性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Interference is when one unit's treatment affects another unit's outcome, common with shared resources (driver pool, inventory), breaking independence.

scenario: 面试官让你具体说明 switchback 的随机化单元和切换节奏。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks you to specify switchback's randomization unit and switching cadence.
q: Switchback 具体怎么随机化？
q_en: How exactly does switchback randomize?
why: 随机化单元是「地理区域 × 时间窗」而不是用户：让一个城市每 30-60 分钟整体在 treatment/控制间切换，同一「城市-时间块」里所有人同一处理，块内没有人被暴露在混合处理下，从而消掉共享供给带来的干扰。
why_en: The unit is region-by-time-window, not the user: a city switches between treatment and control every 30-60 minutes, so everyone in a city-time block shares one arm and within-block interference disappears.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  subgraph 城市A
  T1["0-30min: 处理"] --> C1["30-60min: 控制"] --> T2["60-90min: 处理"]
  end
options: 在地理区域内按时间窗随机：一个城市每 30-60 分钟整体切换处理，块内所有人同一处理
按用户随机分成处理和控制两组，但每隔 30 分钟就把所有用户重新洗牌一次、随机换到另一个分组里去
按订单随机分配处理或控制，每一个订单在下单的那一刻独立抽签、彼此互不影响
按司机随机分成两组，让一半司机永远只服务处理组、另一半永远只服务控制组
options_en: Randomize time windows within a region: a city switches its whole arm every 30-60 minutes, everyone in a block shares one arm.
Randomize users into treatment and control groups, but every 30 minutes reshuffle all users and randomly move them into the other group.
Randomize by order: each order independently draws treatment or control the instant it's placed, unaffected by others.
Randomize by driver into two groups: half always serve the treatment side, the other half always serve the control side.
optionExplanations: 对；城市-时间块整体切换是 switchback 的定义，块内同处理才能消掉共享供给的干扰。
还是按用户随机，同一时刻处理组和对照组共用一个司机池，干扰依旧存在。
按订单随机同样让同时段两种处理共享供给，无法消除干扰。
按司机固定分组会长期割裂供给、制造新的不平衡，也不是 switchback 的时间窗切换。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — switching whole city-time blocks is the definition; one arm per block removes shared-supply interference.
Still user-level: at any instant treatment and control share one pool, so interference remains.
Order-level randomization also has both arms sharing supply at the same time, not removing interference.
Fixed driver groups permanently split supply and create new imbalance — not switchback's time-window switching.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个地理区域在一个时间窗内的整体单元，switchback 让同一块内所有人接受同一处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A city-time block is one region during one time window; switchback gives everyone in that block the same treatment.

scenario: 早晚高峰需求、不同城市供给都不一样，你担心 treatment 恰好都落在高峰或某类城市上，造成偏差。
scenario_en: Rush-hour demand and per-city supply differ, and you worry treatment lands only on peaks or certain cities, biasing results.
q: RBSD（规则平衡 switchback 设计）额外保证了什么？
q_en: What does an RBSD (regular balanced switchback design) additionally guarantee?
why: RBSD 确保每种处理在各个时间槽和各个区域上出现的次数大体相等，从而平衡掉早晚高峰的需求波动和城市间的供给差异——不让 treatment 系统性地压在高峰或某类城市上，避免这些结构性因素冒充成处理效应。
why_en: An RBSD ensures each treatment appears roughly equally across time slots and regions, balancing rush-hour demand swings and city-specific supply so structural factors don't masquerade as the treatment effect.
options: 保证实验只在非高峰时段进行，避开需求波动
保证每种处理在各时间槽和各区域出现次数大体相等，平衡高峰需求与城市供给差异
保证 treatment 组永远比控制组多分到 60% 的时间窗，提高功效
保证切换频率越高越好，把每个时间窗压到 1 分钟
options_en: Guarantees the experiment runs only off-peak, avoiding demand swings.
Guarantees each treatment appears roughly equally across time slots and regions, balancing rush-hour demand and city supply differences.
Guarantees treatment always gets 60% of time windows over control to boost power.
Guarantees the highest possible switching frequency, cutting each window to 1 minute.
optionExplanations: RBSD 不是回避高峰，而是让处理在高峰和非高峰间均衡出现，把高峰这个因素平衡掉。
对；跨时间槽和区域的均衡分配正是 RBSD 的目的，防止结构性波动冒充处理效应。
刻意让某一处理多分流量会引入不平衡，与「平衡」设计的目标相反。
切换频率是另一个取舍问题（太快有残留、太慢块少），RBSD 管的是均衡而非一味加快。
optionExplanations_en: RBSD doesn't avoid peaks; it balances treatments across peak and off-peak so the peak factor cancels.
Correct — balanced allocation across time slots and regions is RBSD's purpose, stopping structural swings from posing as the effect.
Deliberately over-allocating one arm introduces imbalance, opposite to a 'balanced' design's goal.
Switching frequency is a separate tradeoff (too fast leaves carryover, too slow yields few blocks); RBSD governs balance, not raw speed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 规则平衡 switchback 设计：让每种处理在各时间槽与各区域上出现次数大体相等，平衡高峰需求和城市供给差异。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RBSD (Regular Balanced Switchback Design) makes each treatment appear roughly equally across time slots and regions, balancing rush-hour demand and city supply.

scenario: 一个城市从 treatment（涨价）切回控制后，上一窗涨价把司机调度到了别处，下一窗的供给还没恢复。
scenario_en: After a city switches from treatment (surge) back to control, the prior window's surge repositioned drivers, so the next window's supply hasn't recovered.
q: Switchback 的首要失败点是什么，怎么缓解？
q_en: What is switchback's primary failure mode, and how do you mitigate it?
why: 首要失败点是残留效应（carryover）：上一时间窗的处理改变了系统状态（surge 把司机调走），泄漏进下一窗，让相邻块不再独立、污染估计。缓解靠洗脱/缓冲期——切换后丢弃紧接的一段数据不计入分析，再显式建模残留。代价是有效数据变少。
why_en: The primary failure is carryover — a prior window's treatment (surge repositioning drivers) leaks into the next window, so mitigate with washout/buffer periods that discard the immediate post-switch data and by modeling the carryover.
diagram:
flowchart LR T["处理窗: 涨价
司机被调走"] --> W["洗脱/缓冲期
丢弃这段数据"] --> C["控制窗: 供给已恢复
干净测量"]
options: 首要失败点是样本太少；只要多跑几个城市、把每个时间窗拉长、把样本量堆得足够大就能解决，根本不需要任何缓冲期
首要失败点是残留效应：上一窗处理泄漏进下一窗、污染相邻块；用洗脱/缓冲期丢弃切换后数据并建模残留
首要失败点是延迟太高，只要多加几台机器做水平扩容就能把它彻底消除掉
首要失败点是 p 值算错了，换一个更严格的统计检验方法就能修好，跟时间维度无关
options_en: The main failure is too few samples; just run more cities, lengthen each time window, and pile the sample size up high enough to fix it, needing no buffer period at all.
The main failure is carryover: a prior window's treatment leaks into the next, contaminating adjacent blocks; use washout/buffer periods to discard post-switch data and model carryover.
The main failure is high latency, which adding a few more machines for horizontal scaling would completely remove.
The main failure is a miscomputed p-value; switching to a stricter statistical test would fix it, unrelated to the time dimension.
optionExplanations: 多跑城市不解决残留：相邻时间块被上一窗状态污染是时间维度的问题，加城市无济于事。
对；残留是 switchback 最核心的风险，洗脱期丢掉切换后过渡数据、再建模残留，是标准缓解手段，代价是有效块变少。
延迟是服务性能问题，跟实验设计里的时间残留无关。
残留是设计层面的结构污染，不是换检验能修的统计小问题。
optionExplanations_en: More cities won't fix carryover: adjacent time blocks contaminated by the prior window is a temporal issue, unaffected by adding cities.
Correct — carryover is switchback's core risk; washout periods drop transitional post-switch data and modeling carryover is the standard fix, costing usable blocks.
Latency is serving performance, unrelated to temporal carryover in the design.
Carryover is structural design contamination, not a small statistical issue fixable by swapping tests.

termDefinitions.meaning: 上一时间窗的处理改变了系统状态并延续到下一窗，使相邻块不独立、污染估计。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A carryover effect is when a prior window's treatment changes the system state and persists into the next window, making adjacent blocks non-independent.

termDefinitions.meaning: 切换处理后丢弃紧接的一段过渡数据、不计入分析，等系统状态稳定再测量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A washout/buffer period discards the transitional data right after a switch, measuring only once the system settles.

scenario: 设计 switchback 时你要定每个时间窗多长：切太快还是切太慢各有代价。
scenario_en: Designing a switchback, you must set the window length: switching too fast or too slow each has a cost.
q: Switchback 的切换频率该怎么权衡？
q_en: How do you trade off switchback's switching frequency?
why: 切太快：相邻窗的残留效应来不及洗脱、互相污染；切太慢：整个实验能拿到的独立时间块变少、统计功效下降。所以要在「残留污染」和「独立块数量/功效」之间取中间的窗长（常见 30-60 分钟量级），并留缓冲期。
why_en: Too fast leaves carryover contaminating adjacent windows; too slow yields fewer independent blocks and lower power, so pick a middle window length (often 30-60 min) with buffers.
tradeoff: 切太快（残留污染重）vs 切太慢（独立块少、功效低）——在两者间取中间窗长
options: 切换越快越好，窗口越短能拿到的块就越多，功效一定越高，完全没有副作用
切换越慢越好，窗口越长残留效应越小，实验结论一定越可信，完全没有副作用
太快→残留污染相邻窗；太慢→独立块变少、功效下降；取中间窗长并留缓冲
频率无所谓，随便设，只要城市数量够多就能抵消一切
options_en: Faster switching is always better; shorter windows mean more blocks and always higher power, with absolutely no downside.
Slower switching is always better; longer windows mean less carryover and always more trustworthy conclusions, with no downside.
Too fast contaminates adjacent windows with carryover; too slow yields fewer independent blocks and lower power; pick a middle window with buffers.
Frequency doesn't matter; set it arbitrarily as long as you have enough cities to cancel everything.
optionExplanations: 越快块越多但残留来不及洗脱，相邻窗互相污染，功效未必真的更高。
越慢残留小但独立块骤减，功效下降，也不是没有副作用。
对；这是一个双边取舍，中间窗长兼顾残留可控与块数足够，配合缓冲期。
频率直接决定残留和块数两大因素，绝非无所谓，城市多也补不了时间维度的污染。
optionExplanations_en: Faster gives more blocks but carryover can't wash out, so adjacent windows contaminate each other and power may not rise.
Slower reduces carryover but sharply cuts independent blocks and power — not free of downside.
Correct — a two-sided tradeoff; a middle window keeps carryover controllable and blocks sufficient, with buffers.
Frequency directly sets both carryover and block count; it matters, and more cities can't offset temporal contamination.

termDefinitions.meaning: 彼此不受残留污染、可当作独立观测的时间-区域块；块越多统计功效越高。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An independent block is a time-region block free of carryover contamination, usable as an independent observation; more blocks give more power.

scenario: 你要评估一个平台级/国家级的政策变更（比如整个美国上线新反欺诈模型），根本没法把用户随机分成处理/控制两组。
scenario_en: You must evaluate a platform-wide/country-level change (e.g. a new fraud model live across the whole US) where user-level treatment/control randomization is impossible.
q: 无法随机分组时该用哪类方法估因果？
q_en: When randomization is impossible, which method class estimates the causal effect?
why: 用准实验（DiD/合成控制）：全平台上线没有随机对照组，只能用观测数据构造反事实——DiD 拿相似未受影响群体的前后变化作对照，合成控制加权拟合出「合成对照」，代价是要靠可识别假设。
why_en: Use quasi-experimental methods (DiD or synthetic control) that build a counterfactual from observational data when there's no randomized control, at the cost of relying on an identifying assumption.
tradeoff: 准实验（无需随机、能评平台级变更，但依赖可识别假设）vs A/B（干净随机，但这里根本无法分组）
whenOtherWins: 只要还能对用户/单元做随机分组（哪怕分层或按地域），就优先用 A/B 或 switchback，随机化给的因果结论比准实验的假设依赖更稳。
options: 标准 A/B：把全美用户当场随机分成两组，一组切到新反欺诈模型、另一组继续沿用旧模型作为对照跑
准实验（DiD / 合成控制）：用观测数据构造反事实对照来估因果，依赖可识别假设
Interleaving：把新旧反欺诈模型交错作用于同一笔交易
多臂老虎机：在新旧模型间自适应分配用户流量
options_en: Standard A/B: randomly split all US users into two arms on the spot, one switched to the new fraud model and the other kept on the old model as control.
Quasi-experiment (DiD / synthetic control): build a counterfactual control from observational data to estimate the effect, relying on an identifying assumption.
Interleaving: interleave the old and new fraud models on the same transaction.
Multi-armed bandit: adaptively allocate user traffic between old and new models.
optionExplanations: 题目前提就是全平台上线、没法随机分两组，A/B 在这里根本无法实施。
对；无随机时用观测数据构造反事实（DiD 的对照群、合成控制的加权组合）来估因果，代价是要明说并守住可识别假设。
反欺诈是二选一的决策，无法像排序结果那样交错，interleaving 不适用。
bandit 仍要能在用户间分配不同处理；全平台统一上线时没有可分配的对照，用不了。
optionExplanations_en: The premise is a platform-wide launch with no way to split arms, so A/B simply can't run here.

Correct — without randomization you build a counterfactual from observational data (DiD's control group, synthetic control's weighted mix), at the cost of stating and defending an identifying assumption.
Fraud scoring is a single decision that can't be interleaved like ranked results; interleaving doesn't apply.
A bandit still needs to allocate different treatments across users; a uniform platform launch leaves no control to allocate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无法随机分组时，用观测数据和统计假设构造反事实对照来估计因果效应的方法（如 DiD、合成控制）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quasi-experiment estimates causal effects from observational data and statistical assumptions when randomization is impossible (e.g. DiD, synthetic control).

termDefinitions.meaning: 「如果没有这次变更会怎样」的假想结果；准实验的核心是把它估计出来当对照。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A counterfactual is what would have happened without the change; quasi-experiments estimate it as the control.

scenario: 反欺诈新模型只在美国上线、加拿大没上。两国都有共同的季节性波动，你想把模型效应从季节性里剥出来。
scenario_en: A new fraud model launches in the US but not Canada. Both share seasonal swings, and you want to isolate the model's effect from seasonality.
q: 差分-in-differences（DiD）怎么估计处理效应？
q_en: How does difference-in-differences (DiD) estimate the treatment effect?
why: DiD 比较处理组和未处理组各自的「前→后变化」，再相减：从美国的前后变化里减去加拿大的前后变化，共同的季节性趋势被抵消，剩下的就是模型的处理效应。关键可识别假设是平行趋势——若无处理，两地本会走同样的轨迹。
why_en: DiD subtracts the untreated group's before-to-after change from the treated group's, canceling shared trends and leaving the treatment effect, under the parallel-trends assumption.
diagram:
flowchart LR US["美国: 前→后变化"] --> D["相减"] CA["加拿大: 前→后变化"] --> D D --> E["= 处理效应
季节性被抵消"]
options: 只看美国上线前后的指标差，直接当作模型效应
只看上线后美国和加拿大两地的指标差，直接当作模型效应，不管上线前的差距
从美国的前后变化里减去加拿大的前后变化，抵消共同趋势，剩下的即处理效应
把美国和加拿大的所有数据合并求平均，再和历史比
options_en: Just take the US before-vs-after metric difference and call it the model effect.
Just take the after-launch difference between the US and Canada and call it the model effect, ignoring any pre-existing gap.
Subtract Canada's before-to-after change from the US's, canceling shared trends and leaving the treatment effect.
Merge and average all US and Canada data, then compare against history.
optionExplanations: 只看美国前后差会把季节性等共同趋势也算进效应，无法剥离，估计有偏。
只看上线后两地差会把两地本来就存在的固有差异当成效应，同样有偏。
对；两个差再相减（difference-in-differences）正好抵消掉两地共享的时间趋势，孤立出处理效应。
简单合并平均丢掉了处理/对照结构，得不到干净的因果估计。
optionExplanations_en: US before-vs-after alone folds seasonality and shared trends into the effect, biased.
After-launch US-vs-Canada alone treats the two regions' pre-existing gap as the effect, also biased.
Correct — subtracting the two differences (difference-in-differences) cancels the shared temporal trend, isolating the treatment effect.
Merging and averaging discards the treated/control structure and yields no clean causal estimate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 差分中的差分：用处理组的前后变化减去未处理组的前后变化，抵消共同趋势来估处理效应。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DiD (Difference-in-Differences) subtracts the control group's before-after change from the treated group's to cancel shared trends and estimate the effect.

scenario: 你用 DiD（美国上线、加拿大对照）报了一个正效应。评审问：什么情况下这个结论会不成立？
scenario_en: You reported a positive effect via DiD (US treated, Canada control). A reviewer asks: what would make this conclusion invalid?
q: DiD 的可识别假设是什么，什么会推翻它？
q_en: What is DiD's identifying assumption, and what breaks it?
why: 关键假设是平行趋势：若没有上线，美国和加拿大本会沿相同轨迹变化。若同期恰好有一个只打击处理组的并发变化（如美国单独出台新支付法规），它会被 DiD 误算进模型效应，结论就不成立。所以要明说假设并检查是否有只作用于处理组的并发冲击。
why_en: DiD assumes parallel trends — absent treatment, both groups would move identically — and a concurrent change hitting only the treated group (e.g. a US-only regulation) breaks it by being misattributed to the model.
options: 假设是处理组和对照组的样本量必须完全相等；只要两组样本量稍有不等，这个 DiD 结论就直接被推翻
假设是平行趋势（无处理时两组同轨迹）；一个只作用于处理组的并发变化会推翻它
假设是处理组指标必须上升；只要下降就说明方法错了
假设是两组必须在同一时区；时区不同结论就无效
options_en: The assumption is that the treated and control groups must have exactly equal sample sizes; any slight inequality directly overturns the DiD conclusion.
The assumption is parallel trends (absent treatment both move identically); a concurrent change hitting only the treated group breaks it.
The assumption is the treated metric must rise; any decline means the method failed.
The assumption is both groups must be in the same time zone; different zones invalidate it.
optionExplanations: 样本量不等可以统计上处理，不是 DiD 的可识别假设。
对；平行趋势是 DiD 的命门，只打击处理组的并发冲击会伪装成处理效应，必须显式排查。
处理效应可正可负，方向不是假设；DiD 不要求指标必须上升。
时区无关；DiD 的假设是趋势平行，不是时区一致。
optionExplanations_en: Unequal sample sizes are handled statistically and are not DiD's identifying assumption.
Correct — parallel trends is DiD's crux; a shock hitting only the treated group masquerades as the effect and must be checked.
The effect can be positive or negative; direction isn't the assumption, and DiD doesn't require a rise.
Time zones are irrelevant; the assumption is parallel trends, not matching zones.

termDefinitions.term: parallel trends / 平行趋势假设
termDefinitions.meaning: DiD 的核心假设：若没有处理，处理组和对照组的指标本会沿相同轨迹变化；被并发的组别专属冲击推翻。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Parallel trends is DiD's core assumption that, absent treatment, treated and control groups would follow the same trajectory; a group-specific concurrent shock breaks it.

scenario: 你只在伦敦一个城市做了市场干预，没有哪个单一城市能当干净对照，但你有一堆未干预城市的历史数据。
scenario_en: You intervened in one city (London) with no single clean control, but you have historical data for many untreated cities.
q: 合成控制（synthetic control）怎么构造对照？
q_en: How does synthetic control build a control?
why: 把多个未处理单元加权组合，拟合出干预前轨迹贴合处理单元的「合成对照」（如合成伦敦=巴黎0.4+柏林0.35+马德里0.25）；干预后的偏离量就是因果效应，需要长前期和好 donor pool。
why_en: Synthetic control weights several untreated units into a 'synthetic' unit matching the treated unit's pre-intervention trajectory (e.g. synthetic London = Paris 0.4 + Berlin 0.35 + Madrid 0.25); post-launch divergence is the effect.
diagram:
flowchart LR P["巴黎 0.4"] --> S["合成伦敦"] B["柏林 0.35"] --> S M["马德里 0.25"] --> S S --> DIV["干预后偏离
= 因果效应"]
options: 随便挑一个城市当对照就行，谁在地理上离伦敦最近就选谁作对照，完全不用管它干预前的走势是否贴合
把多个未处理单元加权组合成一个前期轨迹贴合伦敦的合成对照，干预后偏离即因果效应
把所有城市数据平均成一条线当对照，不加权
只用伦敦自己干预前的均值当对照，不用其他城市
options_en: Just pick any one city as the control, whichever is geographically nearest to London, without caring at all whether its pre-intervention trajectory matches.
Weight several untreated units into a synthetic control matching London's pre-period trajectory; post-intervention divergence is the effect.
Average all cities into one flat line as the control, with no weighting.
Use only London's own pre-intervention mean as the control, ignoring other cities.
optionExplanations: 单挑一个城市往往前期轨迹对不上伦敦，做不了干净对照，这正是合成控制要改进的。
对；加权拟合出前期贴合的合成对照，真实值与合成值的差就是处理效应，还得看前期数据够不够长、donor pool 选得好不好。
简单平均不保证前期轨迹拟合伦敦，加权组合才能对齐处理单元的历史走势。
只用伦敦自己的前期均值忽略了大盘趋势，等于没有反事实对照。
optionExplanations_en: One nearest city often doesn't match London's pre-period trajectory, giving no clean control — exactly what synthetic control improves.
Correct — a weighted synthetic control matches the pre-period, and the gap between actual and synthetic after intervention is the effect, needing a long pre-period and good donor pool.
A plain average won't match London's pre-trajectory; weighting is what aligns to the treated unit's history.
London's own pre-mean ignores the market-wide trend and provides no counterfactual control.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用多个未处理单元的加权组合拟合出一个前期轨迹贴合处理单元的虚拟对照，干预后的偏离即因果效应。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Synthetic control weights several untreated units into a virtual control matching the treated unit's pre-period, with post-intervention divergence as the effect.

termDefinitions.meaning: 可用于加权合成对照的未处理单元集合；池子越好、越多样，合成对照越可信。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The donor pool is the set of untreated units available to weight into the synthetic control; a richer pool yields a more credible control.

scenario: 平台级变更没法随机时，你在 DiD 和合成控制之间选一个准实验方法。
scenario_en: For a non-randomizable platform-wide change, you choose between DiD and synthetic control.
q: DiD 和合成控制在对照构造与假设上怎么对比？
q_en: How do DiD and synthetic control contrast on control construction and assumptions?
why: DiD 用一个（组）现成的未处理单元做对照，靠平行趋势假设；合成控制用多个未处理单元加权拟合出一个前期贴合的对照，靠前期拟合质量、需要长前期和好 donor pool。当没有任何单一单元的前期趋势与处理单元平行时，合成控制的加权拟合更稳。
why_en: DiD uses a ready untreated group under parallel trends, while synthetic control weights many untreated units to match the pre-period, needing a long pre-period and good donor pool.
tradeoff: DiD（简单、要平行趋势）vs 合成控制（加权拟合前期、无单一平行对照时更稳，但要长前期+好 donor pool）
options: DiD 其实是用多个未处理单元加权拟合出对照、合成控制反而是用单一现成对照，两者的对照构造刚好说反了
两者对照构造其实完全相同，两个方法说到底只是同一件事的不同叫法而已，压根没有区别
DiD 用现成对照组+平行趋势假设；合成控制靠多单元加权拟合前期，还需要好 donor pool
两者都要求能对用户或处理单元事先做好随机分组，只是最后使用的统计公式不太一样而已
options_en: DiD is actually the one weighting multiple untreated units to fit its control, while synthetic control uses a single ready-made control — their control constructions are exactly reversed.
Their control construction is actually completely identical; the two methods are ultimately just different names for the same thing, no real difference.
DiD uses a ready untreated group with parallel trends; synthetic control weights multiple units to fit the pre-period, needing a long pre-period and good donor pool.
Both require being able to randomize users or treatment units into groups ahead of time, differing only slightly in the final statistical formula.
optionExplanations: 说反了：加权拟合是合成控制，现成单一对照是 DiD。
两者对照构造不同——一个现成群体、一个加权合成，假设与数据需求也不同。
对；这正是取舍轴——现成对照+平行趋势 vs 加权拟合前期；没有单一平行对照时合成控制更合适。
两者都是准实验，恰恰用在无法随机时，不需要随机分组。
optionExplanations_en: Reversed: weighted fitting is synthetic control, a single ready control is DiD.
Their control construction differs — a ready group vs a weighted synthetic — as do assumptions and data needs.
Correct — that's the axis: ready control plus parallel trends vs weighted pre-period fitting; without a single parallel control, synthetic control fits better.
Both are quasi-experiments used precisely when randomization is impossible, needing no randomization.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让观测数据能被解读为因果的前提；DiD 是平行趋势，合成控制是前期拟合质量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An identifying assumption is the premise letting observational data be read causally; DiD's is parallel trends, synthetic control's is pre-period fit.

scenario: 用任何准实验方法汇报结论时，评审最想听到你主动说清的一句话。
scenario_en: When reporting any quasi-experimental result, what the reviewer most wants you to state upfront.
q: 汇报准实验结果时必须主动交代什么？
q_en: What must you state upfront when reporting a quasi-experimental result?
why: 必须明说这套方法的可识别假设（DiD 是平行趋势、合成控制是前期拟合），以及什么会推翻它（如只作用于处理组的并发变化）。准实验的可信度全押在假设上，主动摆出假设和它的失效条件，才是负责任的因果汇报。
why_en: State the method's identifying assumption (parallel trends for DiD, pre-period fit for synthetic control) and what would invalidate it, since quasi-experimental credibility rests entirely on that assumption.
options: 只需报出最终估出来的效应数值就够了，可识别假设只是学术细节，工程汇报里完全可以略过不提
明说可识别假设（平行趋势/前期拟合）以及什么会推翻它，因为可信度全押在假设上
只需说明用了多大样本量，假设正确与否不影响结论
强调结果统计显著即可，显著就说明假设一定成立
options_en: Just reporting the final estimated effect number is enough; the identifying assumption is an academic detail an engineering report can skip entirely.
State the identifying assumption (parallel trends / pre-period fit) and what would invalidate it, since credibility rests entirely on it.
Just state the sample size used; whether the assumption holds doesn't affect the conclusion.
Emphasize that the result is statistically significant; significance proves the assumption holds.
optionExplanations: 略过假设等于隐藏了结论最脆弱的地方，评审无法判断这个因果是否可信。
对；准实验没有随机化兜底，主动摆出假设及其失效条件，是它区别于「数据讲故事」的关键。
样本量大不能修复假设不成立带来的偏差，二者是不同层面的问题。
统计显著只说明不是随机噪声，不能证明可识别假设成立，假设错了显著也是偏的。
optionExplanations_en: Skipping the assumption hides the conclusion's weakest point, leaving reviewers unable to judge the causal claim.
Correct — quasi-experiments lack randomization as a backstop, so stating the assumption and its failure conditions is what separates it from just storytelling with data.
A large sample can't fix bias from a broken assumption; they're different levels of problem.
Significance only rules out random noise; it can't prove the identifying assumption, and a broken assumption makes a significant result biased too.

termDefinitions.meaning: 汇报观测性因果结论时主动列出所依赖的可识别假设及其失效条件，供他人质疑。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Assumption hygiene means proactively listing the identifying assumptions a causal claim relies on and what would invalidate them.

scenario: Uber 要测新的动态定价，司机在骑手之间共享。请把从需求到落地缓解的决策链排好。
scenario_en: Uber tests new dynamic pricing with drivers shared across riders. Order the decision chain from requirement to mitigation.
q: 把「共享供给市场测定价」的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the decision chain for testing pricing in a shared-supply marketplace:
steps: 需求：测新定价对完单率的因果影响
识别干扰：共享司机池让用户级随机违背 SUTVA、估计有偏
选 switchback：按地理区域内时间窗随机，块内所有人同处理
面对残留效应代价：上一窗 surge 调走司机泄漏进下一窗
缓解：加洗脱/缓冲期并建模 carryover，代价是有效块变少
why: 决策链：先定需求（测定价因果影响）→ 识别共享供给带来的 SUTVA 干扰 → 选 switchback 按时间-区域块随机消掉干扰 → 认识到它引入残留效应 → 用洗脱期+建模缓解，代价是有效块变少。每一步都由上一步的约束推出。
why_en: Requirement, then spot shared-supply SUTVA interference, choose switchback to block by time-region, accept carryover as its cost, and mitigate with washout plus modeling at the price of fewer usable blocks.
diagram:
flowchart TB
  R["需求: 测定价因果"] --> I["识别 SUTVA 干扰"]
  I --> S["选 switchback"]
  S --> C["残留效应代价"]
  C --> M["洗脱期+建模缓解"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 稳定单元处理值假设：一个单元结果只取决于自己受的处理；共享司机池破坏它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SUTVA (Stable Unit Treatment Value Assumption) says a unit's outcome depends only on its own treatment; a shared driver pool breaks it.

scenario: 把四种失效场景和对应方法的映射背下来，面试里能秒答「该用哪种实验」。
scenario_en: Memorize the four-failure-to-method mapping so you can instantly answer 'which experiment' in an interview.
q: 补全：标准 A/B 四类失效场景对应的实验方法。
q_en: Fill in the experiment method for each of standard A/B's four failure settings.
text: 微小排序质量差异 → {{interleaving}}；短命内容/动态优化/多变体 → {{bandit}}（多臂老虎机）；双边市场共享供给干扰 → {{switchback}}；平台级/国家级无法随机 → {{准实验}}（DiD/合成控制）。
text_en: Tiny ranking-quality gap → {{interleaving}}; short-lived / dynamic-optimization / many-variant → {{bandit}}; two-sided marketplace shared-supply interference → {{switchback}}; platform-wide / non-randomizable → {{quasi-experiment}} (DiD/synthetic control).
why: 四对映射是骨架：interleaving 治微小排序差，bandit 治短命/多变体，switchback 治共享供给干扰，准实验治无法随机。记住场景→方法，面试里能秒对上工具。
why_en: Four mappings anchor the chapter: interleaving for tiny ranking gaps, bandits for short-lived/dynamic/many-variant, switchback for shared-supply interference, quasi-experiments when you can't randomize.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无法随机时用观测数据+假设估因果的方法，如 DiD、合成控制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quasi-experiment estimates causal effects from observational data plus assumptions when randomization is impossible, e.g. DiD, synthetic control.

scenario: 两个都是「不用固定 50/50」的高效方法，但一个测排序器相对好坏、一个在线上边分配边赚。你要说清何时用哪个。
scenario_en: Both beat a fixed 50/50, but one measures relative ranker quality and one allocates live traffic while earning. Clarify when to use which.
q: Interleaving 和 bandit 各解决什么不同的问题？
q_en: What different problems do interleaving and bandits each solve?
why: interleaving 解决「少样本判排序器谁更受偏好」的评估问题，是被试内比较；bandit 解决「在线把流量导向更优 arm、压低后悔值」的分配问题。前者要快速相对信号，后者要边服务边赚，目标不同。
why_en: Interleaving is a within-subject evaluation of which ranker is preferred with few samples, while a bandit is online allocation that shifts traffic to the better arm to minimize regret.
tradeoff: Interleaving（少样本测排序相对好坏）vs bandit（在线自适应分配、最小化后悔值）
whenOtherWins: 只要问题是「在线上多个版本间分配真实流量并最大化累计收益」，就用 bandit；interleaving 只擅长排序器的相对偏好评估。
options: 两者可以完全互换着用，都只是拿来测排序器谁更受欢迎的相对比较方法而已
interleaving 是被试内评估排序器相对偏好；bandit 是在线自适应分配流量、压低累计后悔值
interleaving 负责在线实时分配真实流量，bandit 只做离线的排序效果评估，两者的分工正好说反了
两者都要求固定 50/50，只是分析口径不同
options_en: They're fully interchangeable and both just relative methods for testing which ranker users prefer more, nothing else.
Interleaving is within-subject evaluation of ranker preference with few samples; a bandit is online adaptive allocation minimizing cumulative regret.
Interleaving handles real-time online allocation of live traffic, while bandits only do offline ranking-quality evaluation — the two roles are exactly reversed.
Both require a fixed 50/50 and differ only in how you analyze the data.
optionExplanations: 两者目标不同：interleaving 是评估工具，bandit 是分配策略，不能互换。
对；一个回答「哪个排序器更受偏好」，一个回答「怎么分配线上流量最赚」，各管一段。
方向说反了：interleaving 才是评估、bandit 才是在线分配。
两者都不用固定 50/50——interleaving 是被试内合并、bandit 是自适应分配。
optionExplanations_en: Different goals: interleaving is an evaluation tool, a bandit is an allocation strategy — not interchangeable.
Correct — one answers which ranker is preferred, the other how to allocate live traffic most profitably.
Reversed: interleaving is the evaluation, a bandit is the online allocator.
Neither uses a fixed 50/50 — interleaving merges within-subject and bandits allocate adaptively.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在实验进行中实时决定给每个版本多少真实流量，bandit 属于此类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Online allocation decides in real time how much live traffic each version gets during the experiment; bandits do this.

scenario: 广告投放里，把 50% 流量固定分给一个明显更差的广告变体，每一小时都在白白损失可观营收。
scenario_en: In ad serving, fixing 50% of traffic to a clearly worse ad variant loses meaningful revenue every hour.
q: 「差 arm 的机会成本很高」的动态优化场景该用哪种实验？
q_en: Which experiment fits dynamic optimization where a losing arm's opportunity cost is high?
why: 用多臂老虎机：固定 50/50 的 A/B 会在整个实验期把一半曝光烧在差广告上，机会成本极高；bandit 边学边把流量倾向表现好的广告，把累计后悔值（因没选最优损失的营收）压到最小，正好适配「输不起差 arm」的动态优化。
why_en: Use a multi-armed bandit because a fixed 50/50 A/B burns half the impressions on the losing ad; adaptive allocation minimizes cumulative regret, fitting high-opportunity-cost dynamic optimization.
tradeoff: Bandit（少烧差 arm、最小化后悔值，但固定终点推断难）vs A/B（干净因果，但差 arm 机会成本高）
whenOtherWins: 如果你要的是一个可长期复用、能严格因果归因的绝对结论，或需要干净 p 值上报，宁可承担 A/B 的实验期成本换纯度。
options: 多臂老虎机：边学边把流量倾向好广告，最小化累计后悔值，适配输不起差 arm 的动态优化
标准 A/B：全程固定 50/50 平均分流量，一直等到实验结束再回头选出好广告，简单可靠、什么都不用调
Switchback：按城市时间窗在两个广告间整体切换
Interleaving：把两个广告交错进一个列表比相对偏好
options_en: A multi-armed bandit: learn while shifting traffic to the better ad, minimizing cumulative regret, fitting high-cost dynamic optimization.
Standard A/B: hold a fixed 50/50 even split throughout, wait until the experiment ends to pick the winning ad, simple and reliable with nothing to tune.
Switchback: switch between the two ads by whole city-time windows.
Interleaving: merge the two ads into one list and compare relative preference.
optionExplanations: 对；差 arm 机会成本高时，bandit 的自适应分配直接减少浪费、最小化后悔值，是动态优化的首选。
固定 50/50 意味着整个实验期都在差广告上烧一半流量，机会成本正是这里最痛的点。
switchback 是为共享供给干扰设计的，广告投放没有共享稀缺供给问题，用错工具。
interleaving 只测相对偏好、不最大化营收，也不做在线流量分配，不匹配。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — when a losing arm's opportunity cost is high, a bandit's adaptive allocation cuts waste and minimizes regret, the go-to for dynamic optimization.
A fixed 50/50 burns half the traffic on the worse ad all experiment long — exactly the pain point here.
Switchback is for shared-supply interference; ad serving has no shared scarce supply, so it's the wrong tool.
Interleaving only measures relative preference, doesn't maximize revenue or allocate live traffic — a mismatch.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把流量分给差 arm 而没分给最优 arm 所损失的收益，bandit 就是要压低它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Opportunity cost is the revenue lost by giving traffic to a worse arm instead of the best; bandits minimize it.

scenario: 面试官要你按「随机化单元/设计类型」把这几种方法归类，看你是否理解它们的本质差异。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks you to classify these methods by randomization unit / design type to test whether you grasp their essence.
q: 这几种方法的「设计类型」分别是什么？
q_en: What is each method's design type?
why: 标准 A/B 被试间、interleaving 被试内、bandit 自适应分配、switchback 时间-区域聚类随机、DiD/合成控制观测性；分清随机化单元才能按约束选对方法。
why_en: A/B is between-subject, interleaving within-subject, bandits adaptive, switchback cluster-randomized by time-region, and DiD/synthetic control observational; the randomization unit dictates which method fits.
options: 五种方法都是被试间随机、用相同的显著性公式计算，差别只在最后看哪个业务指标
A/B 被试间、interleaving 被试内、bandit 自适应、switchback 聚类随机、DiD/合成控制观测性
interleaving 和 switchback 都是被试间随机、分组后固定；bandit 和 DiD 都是被试内随机、同一单元反复比较
五种方法都不需要随机化，全靠观测数据和统计假设估计效应，跟做不做 A/B 没有本质区别
options_en: All five use between-subject randomization with the same significance-test formula, differing only in the final business metric you check.
A/B between-subject, interleaving within-subject, bandit adaptive, switchback cluster-randomized, DiD/synthetic control observational.
Interleaving and switchback are both between-subject (assignment fixed after split); bandit and DiD are both within-subject (repeated comparison on the same unit).
None of the five need randomization; all rely on observational data and statistical assumptions, no different from skipping A/B altogether.
optionExplanations: 只有标准 A/B 是被试间；其余在随机化单元或设计类型上各不相同。
对；这条随机化单元/设计类型的主轴决定了该配哪种统计方法，认错设计类型统计推断就会跟着错。
分类刚好颠倒了：同一用户反复对比的是 interleaving，按时间区块整体切换的是 switchback，靠历史数据估计效应的是 DiD。
A/B、interleaving、bandit、switchback 都用随机化，只有 DiD/合成控制是观测性。
optionExplanations_en: Only standard A/B is between-subject; the rest differ in randomization unit or design type.
Correct — this randomization-unit/design-type axis decides which statistical method applies; misclassify it and the inference goes wrong too.
Backwards: repeated comparison on the same user is interleaving, whole time-block switching is switchback, and estimating from historical data is DiD.
A/B, interleaving, bandit, and switchback all randomize; only DiD/synthetic control are observational.

termDefinitions.meaning: 随机化的单元是一个群组（这里是时间×区域块）而非单个用户，用于存在群内干扰的场景。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cluster-randomized means the randomization unit is a group (here a time-by-region block) rather than an individual user, used when within-group interference exists.

tradeoff: 被试间/被试内/自适应/聚类随机 vs 观测性（无随机）——随机化单元不同，可信度和适用边界也不同

scenario: interleaving 说排序器 B 明显更受偏好，有人主张跳过 A/B 直接全量上线 B。
scenario_en: Interleaving says ranker B is clearly preferred, and someone argues to skip A/B and launch B to everyone.
q: 为什么 interleaving 赢了还不能直接跳过 A/B 上线？
q_en: Why can't you skip A/B and launch just because interleaving won?
why: interleaving 是单会话的相对偏好信号，抓不到长期效应：B 可能靠新奇效应短期讨喜、几周后消退，或提升点击却拉低营收/留存。所以它只能当初筛，真正上线要用 A/B 在观察窗里测绝对业务指标和长期行为。
why_en: Interleaving is a single-session relative signal that misses long-term effects like novelty fading or clicks-up-but-revenue-down, so it screens candidates while A/B must confirm absolute long-run impact.
options: 因为 interleaving 的样本量目前还不够大，只要多跑几天、把样本量堆得更充分些、置信区间再收窄一点就能直接全量上线
因为 interleaving 是单会话相对信号，抓不到新奇效应消退、营收留存等长期效果，须靠 A/B 收口
因为 interleaving 只在深夜流量很小的时段才准确有效，白天高峰期的结果完全不可信
不用等，interleaving 只要赢了就代表绝对营收一定更高，可以直接全量上线不用再测
options_en: Because interleaving's sample size is not yet large enough; just run it a few more days, pile up a fuller sample, and narrow the confidence interval a bit before rolling out to everyone.
Because interleaving is a single-session relative signal missing long-term effects (novelty fading, revenue/retention), so confirm absolute impact with A/B first.
Because interleaving is only accurate during low-traffic overnight hours; results during the daytime peak are completely untrustworthy.
No need to wait — as soon as interleaving wins it means absolute revenue is definitely higher, so roll out to everyone without further testing.
optionExplanations: 问题不在样本量：interleaving 样本已够，缺的是绝对指标和长期视角。
对；相对偏好赢不代表营收/留存也赢，长期效应要 A/B 的观察窗才看得到，interleaving 只能初筛。
时段与它无关；局限是「相对+单会话」，不是昼夜。
相对偏好不等于绝对营收，直接全量可能上线一个点击高但赚得少的排序器。
optionExplanations_en: Not a sample-size issue: interleaving already has enough samples; it lacks absolute metrics and a long-run view.
Correct — a relative-preference win isn't a revenue/retention win, and long-term effects need an A/B window; interleaving only screens.
Time of day is irrelevant; the limit is relative and single-session, not day vs night.
Relative preference isn't absolute revenue; launching directly may ship a high-click, low-revenue ranker.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只在一次访问内观测到的偏好，抓不到跨天/跨周的行为变化和长期业务效应。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A single-session signal is a preference observed within one visit, missing cross-day behavioral change and long-term business effects.

scenario: 一个国家级新政（如全美统一上线新排序）已经全量发布，事后老板要一个「它到底有没有用」的因果估计。
scenario_en: A country-level change (a new ranking live across the whole US) already fully launched, and leadership wants an after-the-fact causal estimate of its impact.
q: 全量发布后、想补一个因果估计，最该用什么？
q_en: After a full launch, to recover a causal estimate, what should you use?
why: 已经全量、没有随机对照组，只能用准实验从观测数据构造反事实：若有一个未受影响的相似地区/群体做对照就用 DiD（靠平行趋势），若没有单一平行对照就用合成控制加权拟合前期。别硬报「上线前后简单差」，那会把季节性等趋势算进效应。
why_en: With a full launch and no randomized control, use a quasi-experiment to build a counterfactual — DiD if a comparable untreated region exists, synthetic control otherwise — rather than a naive before-after difference.
tradeoff: 准实验（能补估因果，但依赖平行趋势/前期拟合假设）vs 简单前后差（易做，但把趋势误算成效应）
whenOtherWins: 如果发布前就规划好、还能按地域或分层做随机灰度，那就用 A/B/switchback 拿更硬的随机化结论，而不是事后准实验。
options: 简单看一下全美上线前后的指标差值，直接把这个差当作新排序的因果效应就行，季节性等别的因素都不用管
准实验（有相似未处理地区用 DiD、否则用合成控制）从观测数据构造反事实来估因果
重新对全美用户随机分两组补做 A/B（已全量，无法回退）
用多臂老虎机在新旧排序间自适应分配（已全量，无对照可分配）
options_en: Just look at the before-vs-after metric difference across the US and treat that gap as the new ranking's causal effect, ignoring seasonality and every other factor.
A quasi-experiment (DiD if a comparable untreated region exists, else synthetic control) building a counterfactual from observational data.
Re-randomize all US users into two arms to run an A/B now (already fully launched, can't roll back).
Use a multi-armed bandit to adaptively allocate between old and new ranking (already fully launched, no control to allocate).
optionExplanations: 简单前后差会把季节性、大盘趋势也算进效应，估计有偏，正是准实验要避免的错误。
对；无随机对照时用 DiD 或合成控制构造反事实是标准做法，别忘了明说所依赖的可识别假设。
已经全量上线，没法再把用户拆成看不到新排序的对照组，A/B 无从做起。
bandit 需要能在用户间分配不同处理；全量上线后没有可分配的对照，用不了。
optionExplanations_en: A naive before-after difference folds seasonality and market trends into the effect — biased, exactly what quasi-experiments avoid.
Correct — without a randomized control, DiD or synthetic control to build a counterfactual is standard; just state the identifying assumption.
Already fully launched, you can't carve out a control that never sees the new ranking, so A/B can't start.
A bandit needs to allocate different treatments across users; after a full launch there's no control to allocate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 「若没上线会怎样」的假想结果；准实验从未处理单元的观测数据把它估计出来当对照。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A counterfactual is what would have happened without the launch; a quasi-experiment estimates it from untreated units' observational data as the control.
